note: Four guided starting points (PLAN_FINAL 8.9). Each applies a real app state and says what to look at. 'siteIds' lists the id in real-data mode first, then the sample-mode id. Images are local files with their credit; none is a logo or an AI image.

cards.title: What does a 9-day slip do?
cards.blurb: Delay the landing by nine days at IM-2 and see what it costs in sunlight and contact with Earth.
cards.alt: The Moon's south polar region from above, a grey cratered landscape with the pole at the centre.
cards.credit: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University (LROC), via LROC QuickMap
steps: Opens the Slip explorer at IM-2 with a 9-day slip.
Each bar is a 14-day window that starts that many days after 8 Feb 2027.
Compare the sunlight and DSN-contact bars at +9 days with “on time”, and try “Jump to it” for the best window.

cards.title: Is the Sun up at IM-2, and for how long?
cards.blurb: Stand at the IM-2 site and read the real skyline, the Sun and Earth paths, and the numbers behind them.
cards.alt: The Sun's disk, orange, with a few dark sunspots.
cards.credit: NASA/SDO and the HMI science team
steps: Opens Stand here at IM-2 with a 2 m solar array.
The skyline is the site's real terrain; the dashed lines are the Sun's and Earth's paths over a lunar month.
Under “Numbers for this window” read Sunlit % and Longest night, and press Why? on any of them for the explanation.

cards.title: Why is the pole so different?
cards.blurb: Put a south-pole site, a mid-latitude site and an equatorial site side by side.
cards.alt: A map of the whole Moon in greys and browns showing the dark maria and bright highlands.
cards.credit: LROC colour map (NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit)
steps: Opens Compare with IM-2 (85°S), Chandrayaan-3 (69°S) and Blue Ghost (18°N).
Look at “Longest dark stretch”: near the pole the Sun skims the horizon, so light comes and goes with every ridge.
Blue Ghost has no terrain data, so it is a smooth-Moon estimate and is labelled as one.

cards.title: When can we talk to Earth?
cards.blurb: See when Earth is in view from IM-2 and which Deep Space Network station can listen.
cards.alt: The Earth as seen from space, blue oceans and white clouds with Australia visible.
steps: Scroll to Details and open “Pointing & link”: Earth's range, one-way light time and the Goldstone, Canberra and Madrid lanes.
Open “Windows” for every period when the link is up, and click a row to jump the clock to it.
